title: ASVS Level 2 Contextual Human Assurance
description: Conditional human-verification rules activated only for capabilities explicitly enabled in Magebean project configuration.

rules.title: ASVS 1.2.6 LDAP injection (when ldap is used)

args.review: Human assessment scope for enabled capability "ldap": The application protects against LDAP injection vulnerabilities, or that specific security controls to prevent LDAP injection have been implemented.

messages.manual_review: NOT VERIFIED BY MAGEBEAN CLI. Independent human assessment and documented supporting evidence are mandatory before this requirement can be considered satisfied.

This will prevent a token from being reused with an unintended audience. If the audience identifier is dynamically provisioned, the token issuer must validate these audiences in order to make sure that they do not result in audience impersonation.

rules.title: ASVS 10.1.1 Token minimization (when oauth_oidc is used)

args.review: Human assessment scope for enabled capability "oauth_oidc": Tokens are only sent to components that strictly need them. For example, when using a backend-for-frontend pattern for browser-based JavaScript applications, access and refresh tokens shall only be accessible for the backend.

rules.title: ASVS 10.1.2 Bind authorization transaction (when oauth_oidc is used)

args.review: Human assessment scope for enabled capability "oauth_oidc": The client only accepts values from the authorization server (such as the authorization code or ID Token) if these values result from an authorization flow that was initiated by the same user agent session and transaction. This requires that client-generated secrets, such as the proof key for code exchange (PKCE) 'code_verifier', 'state'or OIDC 'nonce', are not guessable, are specific to the transaction, and are securely bound to both the client and the user agent session in which the transaction was started.
evidence_needed: Relevant design, configuration, implementation, or test evidence

messages.manual_review: NOT VERIFIED BY MAGEBEAN CLI. Independent human assessment and documented supporting evidence are mandatory before this requirement can be considered satisfied.

args.review: Human assessment scope for enabled capability "oauth_oidc": If the code flow is used, the OAuth client has protection against browser-based request forgery attacks, commonly known as cross-site request forgery (CSRF), which trigger token requests, either by using proof key for code exchange (PKCE) functionality or checking the 'state'parameter that was sent in the authorization request.
